subject: Quarterline prep — Homebase notes, wins/risks/asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterline prep — Homebase notes, wins/risks/asks

Team —

Quick pulse ahead of the quarterline review next Wednesday. I pulled a compact "homebase" list for the leadership packet; attach is the working deck (QBR_prep_homebase_v1.pdf). Short version below — please read and flag anything you want moved to the top-line.

WINS
- Production latency improvement: Serving runtime change (v0.9.4) pushed Friday reduced p95 generation time for small completion paths by ~18% across dedicated clusters. Impact: lowers projected token cost for Acme POC by 9%.
- Contract momentum: Acme signaled approval on security questionnaire (see attached filled form) pending final pricing term.

RISKS
- Procurement timeline: Acme procurement needs a signed SOW + vendor packet by 04/10 to make the April billing cycle; ProcureCorp (their SOW handler) requires receiving contract redlines no later than 04/05.
- Canary latency regression risk: the new optimized kernel path has one edge-case for long-context chat (>=8k) that increased tail latency on staging. We have a mitigation (rollback switch + targeted query rewrite) but need a decision on whether to include the mitigation in the ship branch.

ASKS (clear, actionable)
1) Laura — can you confirm executive approval on a one-time onboarding credit of $15k for Acme to accelerate going live? They asked for an ask at the exec level. Need reply by EOD Monday.
2) Karthik — please provide legal/procurement read on timeline and whether we can sign an SOW with a standard Redwood PO clause or if we must follow ProcureCorp's template.
3) Marissa — updated ARR/projection slide with impact assumptions (token-cost lift from latency improvement) — can you drop the numbers into slide 4 and push a v1.1 by noon PT?

Drive link and HubSpot record included in metadata. If we can close the SOW window and confirm the credit, we can commit Acme to Q2 pilot capacity and show up as a QBR win.

Thanks — short replies ok.

Jordan Blake
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

[attachment: QBR_prep_homebase_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterline prep — Homebase notes, wins/risks/asks

Thanks Jordan — good concise summary. Two quick items: 1) I'm ok with the one-time onboarding credit in principle but want a short memo that quantifies expected incremental revenue from the Acme pilot (3-6 month view). Please include downside if they don't convert. 2) On the canary regression: if we can scope the risk to only long-context flows and ship with a max-context flag off by default, I'm supportive as the latency wins are material.

Action: Jordan, can you or Marissa attach the incremental revenue sketch and the specific rollback steps for the kernel path? I want to see the rollback checklist before I sign off on the credit.

Laura Bennett
Chief Product Officer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterline prep — Homebase notes, wins/risks/asks

Jordan / Laura —
Updating slide 4 as requested; numbers below and I've pushed QBR_prep_homebase_v1.1 to Drive (link in metadata). Summary:
- Baseline monthly token spend (Acme pilot): $24k
- Projected token spend w/ latency gains (conservative): $21.8k (9% reduction)
- Estimated incremental margin improvement (gross): ~$1.9k/month; with 3-month conversion probability at 40% this nets ~$2.3k expected ARR over first 12 months after pilot (model attached).

Also attached a short rollback checklist for the kernel canary (called kernel_canary_rollback.txt) — highlights: feature flag off, drain in-flight requests, revert kernel build on serving machines, validate KV cache snapshots. I recommend we keep the canary in staging for one more day and enable a controlled rollout only for <8k context flows.

Next steps I completed:
- Pushed v1.1 of the deck to Drive.
- Attached the revenue sketch and rollback checklist to the folder.

Marissa Cole
VP, GTM Strategy, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[attachment: kernel_canary_rollback.txt (text, 6KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterline prep — Homebase notes, wins/risks/asks — action items consolidated

Thanks all — brief consolidation for the packet and exec decision: 

Decisions/Actions by Monday EOD PT:
- Laura: approve or decline the $15k onboarding credit (deliverable: one-line approval email + attach revenue sketch acceptance).
- Karthik: confirm SOW path (ProcureCorp template vs Redwood template) and confirm whether legal needs any additional vendor docs by 04/05.
- Marissa: finalize slide 4 numbers in v1.1 and add a one-paragraph note on downside assumptions in the notes section.
- Ops/Runtime team (FYI): keep canary in staging 24h; if we see no tail anomalies by 11:59PM PT on Saturday, proceed with controlled rollout for contexts <8k and keep flag off for long-context.

I'll draft the SOW redlines for legal to iterate on once Karthik confirms the procurement path. If Laura approves the credit, I'll add an appendix to the deck with the credit justification and expected conversion metrics.

Short replies welcome; I'll fold responses into the QBR packet Monday morning.

Jordan
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

[attachment: security_questionnaire_filled.pdf (pdf, 250KB)]
